# Apostille Atlas

> State-by-state apostille fees, offices, and mail versus in-person rules, copied from official secretary of state pages, plus apostille versus authentication and online notarization.

Apostille Atlas is an independent reference site published by Atlas Guides. Every fee, rule and coverage claim links to the statute, government office or provider page it came from, and each page shows the date it was last checked. Where a figure could not be confirmed on a source page, the table shows a dash instead of a guess. Some outbound links are affiliate links; they are labeled and never change what a page says.

Last updated: 2026-11-28

## Guides

- [Apostille Finder: Steps, Office and Fee for Your State and Document](https://apostillesteps.com/apostille-finder/): Pick the state that issued your document, the document type and the destination country. Get the steps in order, the office, the fee for your number of documents, and mail versus in-person options, from official state pages. (checked 2026-11-28)
- [Does an apostille expire?](https://apostillesteps.com/does-an-apostille-expire/): An apostille has no expiration date under the Hague Apostille Convention and can’t be refused for its age. What can run out is the receiving country’s time limit on the underlying document. What that means for background checks, vital records and e-Apostilles. (checked 2026-11-28)
- [How to get an apostille in Arizona](https://apostillesteps.com/arizona-apostille/): Arizona apostilles from the Secretary of State: $3 per document, 10 to 20 business days by mail, or a $25 expedite fee for walk-in service in Phoenix or Tucson (up to 6 documents). Check or money order by mail, no electronic apostilles. (checked 2026-11-28)
- [How to verify an apostille: online e-Registers and the issuing office](https://apostillesteps.com/how-to-verify-an-apostille/): How to check that a U.S. apostille is genuine: the states with an online e-Register listed by the Hague Conference (November 2026), what to enter, and who to contact when there is no online search. (checked 2026-11-28)
- [How to get an apostille in Colorado](https://apostillesteps.com/colorado-apostille/): Colorado apostilles from the Secretary of State in Denver: $5 per apostille by mail or drop-off, $15 for expedited walk-in service that is generally done in under an hour, check or money order only, plus a free document review by email before you submit. (checked 2026-11-27)
- [How to get an apostille in Georgia](https://apostillesteps.com/georgia-apostille/): Georgia apostilles come from the Superior Court Clerks’ Cooperative Authority (GSCCCA) in Atlanta, not the Secretary of State: $3 per document, walk-in with no appointment, mail usually one to two business days, and no county certification for notarized documents. (checked 2026-11-27)
- [How to get an apostille in Minnesota](https://apostillesteps.com/minnesota-apostille/): Minnesota apostilles from the Secretary of State in Saint Paul: $5 per document, by mail or by in-person appointment. Minnesota issues only apostilles, whatever the destination country, and notarized documents must show all six elements Minnesota law requires. (checked 2026-11-27)
- [Apostille versus authentication for Hague and non-Hague countries](https://apostillesteps.com/apostille-vs-authentication/): How a U.S. apostille differs from an authentication certificate, what the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention covers, and how New York, California, Texas, Florida, and Massachusetts issue the certificate. (checked 2026-11-26)
- [Get your apostille done for you](https://apostillesteps.com/get-it-done/): Send one short request and an independent apostille service will reply with a quote to handle your state, federal, or embassy authentication for you. (checked 2026-11-26)
- [How to get an apostille in Connecticut](https://apostillesteps.com/connecticut-apostille/): Connecticut apostilles from the Secretary of the State: every order starts in the online apostille system, paper apostilles take 5 to 7 business days and e-Apostilles about 24 hours, documents must be signed or notarized in Connecticut within the last 10 years, and vital records still need a paper apostille. (checked 2026-11-25)
- [How to get an apostille in Maryland](https://apostillesteps.com/maryland-apostille/): Maryland apostilles from the Secretary of State in Annapolis: $5 per document, by mail or by scheduled appointment, with notarized documents certified first by the Clerk of the Circuit Court in the county where the notary is commissioned. (checked 2026-11-25)
- [How to get an apostille in Michigan](https://apostillesteps.com/michigan-apostille/): Michigan apostilles and certificates of authority from the Office of the Great Seal: $1 per document, by mail to Lansing or by appointment at nine offices, no expedited service, plus the true copy statement rules for diplomas, transcripts, court papers, and background checks. (checked 2026-11-25)
- [How to get an apostille in Missouri](https://apostillesteps.com/missouri-apostille/): Missouri apostilles, authentications, and notary certifications from the Secretary of State: the $10 fee per notary or official, the $100 adoption cap, same-day walk-in service in Jefferson City and three branch offices, and how to prepare birth, marriage, divorce, and school documents. (checked 2026-11-24)
- [How to get an apostille in Pennsylvania](https://apostillesteps.com/pennsylvania-apostille/): Pennsylvania apostilles and certifications from the Department of State in Harrisburg: the $15 per-document fee, the North Office Building walk-in counter, the mailing address, current mail processing, and the signer rules that get documents rejected. (checked 2026-11-24)
- [How to get an apostille in Washington State](https://apostillesteps.com/washington-apostille/): Washington State apostilles from the Secretary of State: $15 per document, standard (7 to 10 business days), expedited ($100 per 10 documents, 2 to 3 days), and same-day in-person service in Tumwater or Cheney ($150 for the first 10), plus the document rules for vital records, school records, and background checks. (checked 2026-11-24)
- [Apostille Done-Right Checklist Pack: Flowchart, Document Checklists and Cover Letters](https://apostillesteps.com/kit/): A 14-page pack for getting an apostille or embassy legalization right the first time: a Hague vs. non-Hague flowchart, checklists for vital, court, notarized, school, business and federal documents, three fill-in cover letters, and a quick reference for eight state offices plus the U.S. Department of State. (checked 2026-11-23)
- [Hague Apostille Convention countries: full list with U.S. status](https://apostillesteps.com/apostille-countries/): All 129 Hague Apostille Convention countries other than the U.S., with the date the Convention took effect, whether it applies with the United States, and which countries still need embassy legalization. (checked 2026-11-23) Includes 129 linked sub-pages.
- [How to get an apostille in New Jersey](https://apostillesteps.com/new-jersey-apostille/): New Jersey apostille and certification: the $25 standard and $40 expedited fees, the required online order, 12 to 20 business day mail processing, and Trenton walk-in service from the Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services. (checked 2026-11-23)
- [How to get an apostille in North Carolina](https://apostillesteps.com/north-carolina-apostille/): North Carolina apostille, authentication, and authority certificates: the $10 fee, the Raleigh mailing and walk-in addresses, the wet-signature translation rule, school-document notarization, and the post-April-2000 signature rule. (checked 2026-11-23)
- [How to get an apostille in Virginia](https://apostillesteps.com/virginia-apostille/): Virginia apostille and Great Seal authentication: the $10 fee ($5 for extra same-signer documents), the 12-month rule, appointment-only Richmond service, mail times, and why Virginia will not authenticate eNotary documents. (checked 2026-11-23)
- [Online notarization (RON) for apostille documents](https://apostillesteps.com/online-notarization-for-apostille/): How remote online notarization relates to a U.S. apostille, what Texas requires when it apostilles a RON document, and which official pages do and do not address online notarization. (checked 2026-11-23)
- [Who issues apostilles in each U.S. state, plus online apostille verification](https://apostillesteps.com/apostille-offices-by-state/): The designated apostille authority for all 50 states, D.C., and U.S. territories, from the U.S. designation filed with the Hague Conference, with links to the states that let you verify an apostille online. (checked 2026-11-23)
- [How to get an apostille in California](https://apostillesteps.com/california-apostille/): California apostille: the official $20 fee, $6 in-person special handling, Sacramento and Los Angeles offices, mail addresses, and current processing dates from the Secretary of State. (checked 2026-11-22)
- [How to get an apostille in Florida](https://apostillesteps.com/florida-apostille/): Florida apostille and notarial certification: the official $10 or $20 fee, Tallahassee walk-in service, mail addresses, and current processing dates from the Division of Corporations. (checked 2026-11-22)
- [How to get an apostille in Massachusetts](https://apostillesteps.com/massachusetts-apostille/): Massachusetts apostille and certification: the official $6 fee, Boston counter limits, Springfield and Fall River offices, and the two-to-three-week mail time from the Secretary of the Commonwealth. (checked 2026-11-22)
- [How to get an apostille in New York](https://apostillesteps.com/new-york-apostille/): New York apostille and certificate of authentication: the official $10 fee, Department of State offices, same-day walk-in limits, and mail instructions, from the official DOS page. (checked 2026-11-22)
- [How to get an apostille in Texas](https://apostillesteps.com/texas-apostille/): Texas universal apostille: the official $15 fee, adoption fee cap, Austin in-person rules, drop-box timing, and mail turnaround, from the Secretary of State. (checked 2026-11-22)
